component: geometry (centre-lines) of the two large luminous arcs

coordinate_convention.measurement_frame: pixel-index: integer coordinate = centre of that pixel, x right, y down, canvas 0..1023
coordinate_convention.svg_user_space: SVG_user = pixel_index + 0.5 for a 1024 viewBox rendered at 1024px
coordinate_convention.verified_by: rendered a line at SVG x=500 sw=8 with tools/render.py; the same estimator measured it at pixel-index 499.5000 +- 0.0000, width 8.000
coordinate_convention.warning: every sub-pixel number in docs/stage1_findings.md is in the pixel-index frame too; +0.5 must be added to all of them when writing SVG

method.ridge_estimator: perpendicular cross-sections through the R channel, bilinear, 0.2px steps, +-26px; pedestal = cubic polynomial fitted to the wings |u| in [5,16]; centre = midpoint of the two 50%-of-plateau crossings of the pedestal-subtracted profile. The core is a ~6-8px plateau with ~1px edges, so the two-edge midpoint is the natural centre-line estimator and is immune to the (bright) plateau shape.
method.why_R_channel: G and B clip at 255 along the cores (1198/1979 px) while R peaks at 254 in exactly one pixel. Chroma is heavily subsampled (within-2x2-block variance: Y 16.3, Cb 0.047, Cr 0.147), so R = full-res luma + a smooth chroma term: its edge positions agree with Y/G to 0.01-0.05px.
method.sampling: uniform in the parameter of a preliminary ellipse (1.15px arc-length steps), which automatically gives perpendicular cross-sections and so removes the shallow-slope problem at the tips; no row/column scanning needed.
method.flare_handling: the flare raises a strongly curved pedestal over y~420-660. Injection test: adding the measured wing polynomial (0.0235u^3 - 0.167u^2 - 7.52u) to clean cross-sections biases a linear-pedestal estimator by -0.096px but an order>=3 pedestal estimator by only +0.011px, so the cubic pedestal is used everywhere. The correction it applies is +0.13..+0.18px (inward) over y in [440,620] and <0.01px elsewhere. No rows are discarded.
validation: two independent estimators (perpendicular cross-sections vs pure row/column scans with no oblique interpolation) agree to 0.050px RMS, max 0.155px, with no trend in y (all bands within +-0.02px)
the frame's top edge, measured with the same estimator, is straight to 0.034px RMS over x in [300,740] - that is the demonstrated precision floor
synthetic step-pair (rendered line): centre recovered to +-0.0000px and width to 8.000/8 exactly
harmonic decomposition of the residual reaches a floor of 0.055px (L) / 0.063px (R) - the per-point noise
end-to-end: the recommended paths were rendered with tools/render.py and re-measured; see validation_render
method.per_point_uncertainty: spread over 10 estimator variants (frac 0.4/0.5/0.6, pedestal order 3/4/5, wing 13/16/20, channels R/Y/G): <0.01px over most of the arc, <=0.03px near the tips, <=0.05px in the flare band. Point-to-point noise floor 0.055-0.063px.

apex_left_pixelindex.note: x is model-free (local polynomial of x(y), stable to 0.04px over windows +-50..180px and degrees 2-4). y is nearly unmeasurable: x changes by <0.01px within +-3px of the apex.

headline_numbers.waist_note: gap(y) = x_R - x_L has a parabolic minimum of 79.24-79.32px at y=517.1-517.5 (window-dependent); curvature d2gap/dy2 = 1.90e-3 /px, i.e. the gap is only 0.3px wider 20px away from the waist. The curves never touch.
headline_numbers.mirror_axis_note: 504.498 from an orthogonal-distance fit of the reflected left ridge onto the right ridge; 504.546 from mean mid(y) over y in [100,620]; 504.565 from the apex midpoint. NOT the canvas centre (512) and NOT the frame centre (508.54).
headline_numbers.arcs_symmetry_axis_y_note: each curve's own best up/down symmetry axis, found model-free by minimising x(y0+d)-x(y0-d); identical for both curves (514.85). This is 2.3px BELOW the frame centre y=512.53. The apex/waist sits 2.5px lower still (517.3) because both curves bulge inward near the waist relative to their own best ellipse.

circle.verdict: excluded (5-6x worse than an ellipse; max residual 5.4-6.1px)

general_conic.note: the unconstrained conic converges to exactly the rotated-ellipse solution; no extra freedom is used, so 'general conic' buys nothing over 'rotated ellipse'

superellipse.verdict: helps the left curve a lot (0.33->0.19) and the right one not at all - so it is not the construction, it is just another way of absorbing the same shape error

ellipse_split_ry.verdict: for the right curve this (ry differing above/below the centre) beats the rotation; same story - the right curve is up/down asymmetric and several 5-parameter models can absorb it

single_cubic_bezier_free.verdict: no better than an ellipse arc despite 8 parameters - a single cubic cannot follow a 132 deg arc

two_cubic_beziers_at_apex.verdict: THE JUSTIFIED MODEL. Reaches the 0.055-0.063px noise floor to within 30%; every conic leaves a smooth 4-5 lobe +-0.4px residual that no 5th or 6th parameter removes.

H1_pure_mirror_about_x_504.498.interpretation: mirror-symmetric to within +-0.25px for y in [90,620]; real departures up to ~1px for y in [620,930]. The asymmetry is concentrated in the bottom third.

H2_180deg_rotation_about_504.503_514.772.verdict: worse - the pair is a mirror pair, not a rotational copy

H3_mirror_plus_rotation.verdict: no net relative rotation between the two curves (0.00 +- 0.05 deg)

H4_mirror_plus_rotation_plus_yshift.verdict: a near-degenerate pair of parameters; only a partial description of the bottom-third asymmetry

own_updown_symmetry.interpretation: A(d) = x(y0+d) - x(y0-d). The LEFT curve is nearly up/down symmetric (<=0.7px); the RIGHT curve is not (up to 1.8px). That asymmetry is what the ellipse fit converts into an apparent tilt.

mirror_symmetry.verdict: Real design/artwork asymmetry, not measurement bias: mid(y) is reproduced to <0.03px by every estimator variant (frac 0.3-0.7, pedestal order 1-5, wings 12-22, channels R/Y/G), and the two independent estimators agree to 0.05px. It is however confined to y>620 and is at most ~1px, so a strictly mirrored construction is a defensible simplification (it costs ~1px at the two bottom tips only).

tilt_question.answer: The right curve's ~+1.6 deg preference is REAL as a fit result but is NOT a rigid tilt of the curve, and it is not an artefact of the excluded flare rows.

flare_rows_are_irrelevant.note: rot(deg) for the right curve; excluding the flare band changes it by <0.11 deg

the_parameter_is_ill_conditioned.note: truncating the y range swings the fitted rotation from -24 deg to +11 deg while the RMS improves, because a rotation can absorb the (much larger) non-elliptical part of the shape. At matched truncated ranges the two sides prefer nearly equal-and-opposite angles, which is what a mirror pair must do.

evidence.direct_measurement: the best rigid rotation mapping the reflected left ridge onto the right ridge is -0.005 deg (H3), i.e. zero. The direct up/down-symmetry test shows the LEFT curve is symmetric about y=514.85 to 0.37px RMS while the RIGHT is not (0.95px RMS).

tilt_question.recommendation: Do not model either arc as a tilted ellipse in the belief that the artwork is tilted. Use rot=0 for both if using ellipses and accept RMS 0.33/0.47px; or use rot=-0.34/+1.59 purely as best-fit numbers (RMS 0.32/0.22) knowing they are absorbing shape error; or use the 2-cubic Bezier (RMS 0.09) and the question disappears.

ellipse_centre_vs_frame_edge_midpoint.verdict: NO coincidence. cx is individually meaningless (sigma ~7-9px, correlation with rx = -1.000), so 'cx = frame side edge' cannot be excluded for the left curve on cx alone (1.2x worse RMS) - but the vertical halves of the claim fail hard: forcing cy = frame centre y (512.53) makes the fit 2.4-3.7x worse (RMS 1.16-1.21px). The arcs' own symmetry axis is y=514.85, 2.3px below the frame centre.

ellipse_vertical_extremes_vs_frame.verdict: NO. The ellipses' vertical extremes fall 13-17px inside the frame top and 9-13px inside the frame bottom, i.e. 2-4 sigma away, and pinning them costs a factor 2.8-3.9 in RMS. ry = frame half-height (478.65) is also rejected (1.6x).

where_the_ellipse_would_meet_the_corner_.note: at |t| = 1.36-1.42, i.e. 12-16 deg of arc beyond where the stroke has already faded to nothing

tips_and_fade.note: the core width stays 5.9-6.2px right out to the last detectable signal, so the tips are an OPACITY fade, not a geometric taper; the path can be drawn to its full extent and faded photometrically.

last_credible_core.caveat: this last one may be contaminated by the frame's bottom-right corner; treat |t|<=1.21 as the trustworthy extent

tips_and_fade.recommended_path_endpoints: the amp0_extrapolated points (used for the svg strings below). The 2-6% tail continues ~12-25px further along the arc; if the lead's glow model fades the stroke smoothly it is better to extend the path to |t| ~ 1.21 and let opacity reach 0 there, otherwise a hard line-end will be visible.

stroke_width_profile.note: not my component, but measured from the same cross-sections and it is geometry: the core is NOT constant width.
stroke_width_profile.verdict: the taper (+34% at the 50% level, +38% at the 80% level) has the same relative amplitude at both levels, so it is real width variation and not a glow artefact: ~6.0px at the tips, ~8.2px at its widest near y=580-620, and it is NOT centred on the waist (y=517).

model_verdict.summary: Neither arc is a conic. An axis-aligned ellipse leaves a smooth, even-in-y, 4-5 lobe residual of +-0.4px (RMS 0.33 left / 0.47 right, max 0.9/1.3). Adding rotation, a general conic, a superellipse exponent, or a split ry each removes only part of it and each picks a different part - a sure sign that the extra parameter is absorbing model error, not measuring a real degree of freedom. Two cubic Beziers joined at the apex with a vertical tangent (12 parameters) reach RMS 0.083/0.093px on the high-quality point set, i.e. the measurement noise floor. That is almost certainly how the artwork was drawn: three anchors (top tip, apex, bottom tip) with a vertical handle at the apex.
not_justified: rotation of either ellipse (the parameter swings -24..+11 deg with the fitted y-range)
the general-conic 5th parameter (it converges to the rotated ellipse)
a superellipse exponent (helps L, not R)
the individual values of cx and rx: corr(cx,rx) = -1.000, sigma 9.5px each, while cx+rx (the apex) is good to 0.18px

well_conditioned_combinations.method: block bootstrap, 300 resamples of 60-point contiguous blocks (blocks, because the residuals are smooth model error, not white noise); values are [mean, sigma] of the axis-aligned fit
well_conditioned_combinations.note: the model-free apex x (464.94 / 544.19) is 0.48px/0.31px inward of the best-fit-ellipse apex; that is the non-conic waist bulge, not a fitting error

residual_vs_y_axis_aligned_ellipse.sign: positive = the measured ridge lies closer to the icon centre than the model

harmonic_dof_test.note: RMS after removing harmonics in the ellipse angle up to order k: ~10 degrees of freedom in total are needed to describe each curve to its noise floor, consistent with a 2-segment cubic path and inconsistent with any 4-6 parameter primitive

validation_render.method: each candidate was written as an SVG path (with the +0.5 offset), stroked white sw=7 on black, rendered by tools/render.py (resvg) at 1024, and the ridge re-extracted with the same estimator; the numbers are the distances from the re-extracted ridge to the reference ridge polyline
validation_render.note: these end-to-end numbers reproduce the fit statistics, which validates the whole chain including the +0.5 coordinate convention and the renderer

implied_waist_per_model.warning: both ellipse options render the waist 0.79px TOO WIDE and 2.5px too high. The waist sits right against the central flare, so if the lead uses ellipse arcs it is worth nudging each apex inward by ~0.4px (e.g. rx -> rx+0.4 with cx fixed) at the cost of ~0.1px elsewhere.
